source_text: Uh oh, codex-18 looks stuck, I wonder if that's a context-exhausted bug.  I had just submitted an idea about a new approach they could take but the REPL says "starting" for around 80s

reply_text:
㊥ (codex-18 looks stuck) codex-18 isn't stuck. At 22:15:43 it was preparing a response to one of your messages, so it's working now, not hung on a full context.

㊬ (what I checked)
- **First turn:** an invocation for one of your messages started at 22:12:46. It last ran a shell command at 22:15:10, so the "starting" you saw was a turn that was running, just slow to show it.
- **Second turn:** a new invocation, also for a message from you, started at 22:15:24. At 22:15:43 it was at "preparing response". If you sent your idea twice, codex-18 will probably answer both.
- **Queue:** it has 19 queued jobs. A backlog of earlier bells may explain why turns show up late.

㊟ (context exhaustion) The agent record can't show how full codex-18's context is. A full context would show up as an error or an empty reply when this turn ends, not as a turn that never starts.

(timeouts) `psweep.py` can now take a file of constant names and a longer timeout. It's rerunning the seven timed-out probes at 11a8074 with 7 workers and a 90-minute limit, as `bg-1791054231322-127`.
- I didn't park on it. Its results should be in by the time the first Codex job reports back, and I'll read them then.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(Lisp side, so you know where it stands) Since my last report:
- codex-19 has committed Python's `ast` classes in the Lisp image, built from my schema.
- I committed a test file of real metaclass cases (903b5cf). It is 51 cases cut unchanged from ast.py and lean_py, with a self-check showing that each of the six metaclass methods, if removed, changes some case result.
- Those cases fail in Lisp as expected for now, because the runtime doesn't support metaclasses yet. That support is codex-19's next piece of work. After it, the next gate (G1) is module start-up code running in the image.
- So the image is still a few steps from running a declaration probe, and the new workflow can't be tried yet.
